To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
saxophonists can produce strong tract resonances, that these resonances are used in advanced playing techniques, but that in standard playing the tract resonances are not used to tune the instrument.

the impedance of the tract resonator of the saxophone is tuned by experienced players during bugling, in the high range, and for multiphonics, and that in all other cases, including normal playing of the standard saxophone range, the frequency of the playing note lies close to the impedance peak of the combination of the tract and bore resonators in series with the reed.
experienced saxophonists can use their vocal tracts as resonators to tune their notes, but only in the very high and altissimo registers and when producing multiphonics and pitch bending.

the impedance of the mouth cavity is tuned by the saxophonist to select notes in the high register and in multiphonics, but not in the normal register.
the vocal tract is tuned by saxophonists to select the notes played and to produce pitch-bending in advanced techniques.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tract resonances are tuned in the very high and low ranges, in multiphonics, and in pitch bending, and that the tract resonator is not used in the standard range.
saxophonists use the tract to tune the impedance seen by the reed in the mouthpiece, and that this impedance is the sum of the impedance of the tract and the instrument bore.
the saxophonist is able to tune the vocal tract to select the note, but not to tune the tract impedance to match that of the instrument.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the saxophone is a reed instrument in which the player tunes the vocal tract resonances to select the note played.

the impedance spectrum of the vocal tract is an important determinant of the playing frequencies of the saxophone, and the experienced player can tune this spectrum to select the note played, to produce multiphonics and to bend pitch.
the saxophonist tunes his/her tract resonances in order to produce the highest quality notes in the very high register of the instrument and in the multiphonics.
